reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but independently implements occurrence eligibility in three consumers.

duplication.why: Daily skip-versus-shift decisions are repeated across getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, which also repeats its holiday adjustment branch.

placement.why: Holiday matching belongs in shared/schedules.ts and handler registration belongs in app.ts, but shared occurrence policy is spread into server handlers.

scope.why: All edits concern the requested schedule rules, range handler, configuration field or associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate multiple policy implementations, unexplained occurrence and range bounds, and existing budget callers that do not receive the new policy.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently decide occurrence eligibility around getDateWithSkippedWeekend instead of sharing the scheduling policy implemented in getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily/weekend/holiday policy appears as a local filtering function in getNextDate, a filter/map pipeline in getUpcomingDates and nested branches in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter; getNextDate adds daily-specific take selection, conditional filtering and an adjustment guard, while both server date-list handlers independently implement the daily exception.
